title: Edge-compatible SDK shim: unified pagination/streaming/retry API for Python, TS, Go
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Redwood SDK teams maintain separate idiomatic clients for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Customers building edge/embedded integrations and server-side middle tiers have asked for a single, predictable client surface that handles pagination, streaming, and retry/backoff semantics consistently across languages while being tolerant of edge networks (intermittent connectivity, proxies, limited memory).

Goals: Provide a lightweight 'shim' layer distributed in each language that:
- Exposes a single logical API for paginated list calls, streaming chat/generation, and long-poll endpoints.
- Encapsulates recommended retry/backoff policies with sensible defaults and overrides.
- Supplies resume semantics for streaming and paginated fetches using compact tokens.
- Preserves backward compatibility with existing SDKs via a compatibility mode toggle.

Scope (in-scope): pagination cursors and resumability, streaming resume tokens, client-side retry helpers (idempotency keys and backoff jitter), language idiomatic bindings (Python/TS/Go), acceptance criteria, migration guide, tests and telemetry.

Non-goals (out-of-scope): server protocol redesigns, full transport-layer (gRPC) replacements, automatic server-side replay of non-idempotent operations.

API contract (high level):
- list_items(request): returns a PaginatedIterator with methods next_page() and items() and exposes a resume_token when paused.
- stream_responses(request): returns a StreamReader with read_event() and a checkpoint() that returns a resume_token which can be passed to resume_stream(token).
- with_retry(fn, options): helper wrapper that applies idempotency_key management for unsafe operations and uses exponential backoff + full jitter for transient errors.

Compatibility modes: "legacy" (v1) mirrors current SDK behavior; "unified" (v2) enables cursor-first pagination, resumable streaming tokens, and the new helper surface. Default: start in "legacy" for GA migration window; enable opt-in "unified" in beta.

Observability & metrics: track SDK-level metrics for retry_count, resumed_streams, resumed_pages, avg_time_between_resume_and_complete, memory_peak_per_stream. Add traces linking SDK resume tokens -> server trace-id for debugging.

Rollout plan: alpha internal SDKs (eng + solutions) -> external beta with opt-in flag -> GA with migration docs and codemods.

Examples (pseudocode):
Python:
client = EdgeClient(mode='unified')
iterator = client.list_items({'page_size': 100})
for item in iterator.items():
    process(item)
# pause, persist resume token
token = iterator.resume_token
# later
iterator = client.list_items_resume(token)

TS:
const client = new EdgeClient({compat: 'unified'})
const stream = await client.streamResponses(req)
for await (const ev of stream) { /* ... */ }

Acceptance testing: unit + integration harness that injects network faults and verifies resume correctness and idempotency behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs implement unified API with parity for core features (pagination, streaming, retries)
Paginated iterator exposes stable resume_token; resuming from token yields deterministic continuation (no duplicates or gaps) in 99.9% of test cases
Streaming API supports checkpoint() tokens; resuming a stream replays from last checkpoint without client-side state corruption
Retry wrapper applies exponential backoff with full jitter and default retryable error set; customers can override policy
Non-idempotent operations require explicit idempotency_key via helper and are not retried silently
Compatibility mode toggle exists and migration guide published; default to legacy for first GA release
SDK telemetry emits retry_count, resumed_streams, resumed_pages, and ties resume tokens to server trace IDs for debugging
Performance: memory usage per active stream under 16MB on average for typical chat workloads; latency amplification due to shim <5%
Documentation: PRD, migration guide, language examples, and a cookbook entry for common patterns published
Security: security review completed and KMS usage for idempotency_key storage documented
decisions: Use compact base64 resume tokens that encode server cursor + client epoch + checksum
Default retry policy: 100ms initial, 2x multiplier, max 5s, full jitter, 5 attempts for transient errors
Expose explicit idempotency_key helper rather than auto-generating for non-idempotent endpoints
Compatibility path: preserve existing client surface under 'legacy' namespace; new surface under 'unified' namespace to reduce breaking changes
tradeoffs: Holding small buffers to enable deterministic resume increases client memory usage slightly versus fully streaming pass-through
Adding resume tokens requires minimal server support (cursor surface) but avoids large wire protocol changes
Unified API complexity vs language ergonomics: we favor a thin shim that delegates to language idioms rather than forcing identical signatures across languages
